ai.title: Add MRR calculation script
ai.summary: Added scripts/calculate-mrr.ts to compute Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) and Annual Run Rate (ARR) via Stripe API. The script paginates active subscriptions, filters out those scheduled for cancellation (cancel_at_period_end), and sums only licensed base fees. Exposed as bun run --cwd scripts mrr in scripts/package.json. Documented in backend/src/billing/billing.knowledge.md.

eli5.text: You can now check how much steady monthly income your paying subscribers are bringing in by running a simple command. The new tool asks Stripe for every active subscription, skips anyone whose subscription is set to end at the next billing cycle, and adds up just the base subscription price. It then shows both the monthly total and a year-long estimate. This is available today and documented in the billing guide. What you'd notice if you looked: the system already excluded usage-based charges and canceled subscriptions, and now also skips any subscription scheduled to cancel at period end, making the revenue figure reflect only ongoing, committed subscriptions.

ai.title: Persistent PTY shell replaces childprocess for terminal commands
ai.summary: Terminal command execution in npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts switched from `child_process.spawn` to a persistent `node-pty` shell. This unifies stdout/stderr into a single stream, matching real terminal behavior and simplifying output parsing. The CLI and tool handlers now rely on `resetPtyShell` for initialization and timeout recovery, removing separate stderr handling. Jest testing infrastructure added via `npm-app/jest.config.js` and `package.json` devDependencies.

eli5.text: The assistant's terminal command system now uses a real, always-on shell instead of launching a fresh process for each command. This means command output appears exactly as it would in a normal terminal, with errors mixed naturally into the same stream as regular output. The system also gained a test framework and helper functions to verify the terminal behaves correctly, plus handling for stopping commands that take too long.

ai.title: Windows PTY spawns cmd.exe outside PowerShell
ai.summary: npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts createPty now calls detectShell() to pick powershell.exe or cmd.exe on win32, replacing hardcoded powershell.exe. New npm-app/src/util/detect-shell.ts probes $PSVersionTable, COMSPEC, and parent process via wmic/ps to resolve the active shell. Scope limited to CLI tool handlers; Web/Desktop unaffected. Unix path still defaults to bash.

eli5.text: When you run a command-line tool on Windows, it now automatically uses the same shell program you're already working in instead of always forcing PowerShell. If you're in Command Prompt, it opens Command Prompt; if you're in PowerShell, it uses PowerShell. The tool now checks what shell is currently running before starting a new terminal session.

ai.title: Add German error detection to handleRunTerminalCommand
ai.summary: handleRunTerminalCommand now checks for additional German error strings indicating command not found in PowerShell. This improves error handling for non-English locales. Affects npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts.

eli5.text: If you use the assistant in a German-language locale and run a terminal command that doesn't exist, the error message is now correctly recognized instead of being missed. Previously, certain German phrases meaning 'command not found' were not caught, so the assistant could appear to hang or give a confusing response. Now, when PowerShell returns one of those additional German error strings, the assistant handles it the same way it already did for English, so you get a proper error instead of silence. This is already live today.

eli5.text: On January 7, 2025, the team behind the AI coding helper you use shipped a behind-the-scenes update. German-speaking users also get better error messages when a command can't be found. This update is already live, and anyone using the assistant on Windows or writing in German will get the smoother experience automatically.

ai.title: Revert Windows cmd.exe shell detection
ai.summary: Reverts Windows shell detection logic in `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts`. `createPty` now hardcodes `powershell.exe` for `win32` and `bash` otherwise, removing the `detectShell` import. Deletes `npm-app/src/util/detect-shell.ts` which previously used `execSync` and `wmic` to identify parent shells. Scope limited to CLI tool handlers; no user-facing config changes.

eli5.text: When the software opens a terminal window on a Windows computer, it now always uses PowerShell instead of trying to figure out which shell program you were already using. It no longer runs extra checks to detect whether you were in PowerShell or the older Command Prompt, and it has stopped defaulting to Command Prompt when it couldn't tell. The effect for you is that any automated tool that opens a terminal on Windows will start PowerShell, regardless of what shell you had open before; on Mac and Linux the behavior stays the same.
